User story: As a visitor, I want a clear app title and explanation so I know what workflow I am opening.
Expected behaviour: The React page renders the Petri Net Workflow Demo heading and summary text.

User story: As a visitor, I want quick feature highlights so I can understand available capabilities before interacting.
Expected behaviour: The React page shows Interactive flow, Decision checkpoints, and Static fallback chips.

User story: As a visitor, I want to open the full static demo directly so I can use it outside the embedded frame.
Expected behaviour: The primary Open static fallback action links to ./static.html.

User story: As a visitor, I want a back link so I can return to the app index.
Expected behaviour: The Back to app index action links to ../../index.html.

User story: As a visitor, I want the static workflow embedded on the React page so I can start exploring immediately.
Expected behaviour: The React page embeds an iframe titled Petri Net Workflow Demo with src ./static.html.

User story: As a static-demo user, I want links back to the React version and app index so I do not get stranded.
Expected behaviour: The static page has React version and Back to app index links.

User story: As a planner, I want the initial Petri-net state visible so I can see available work.
Expected behaviour: On load, the status is Ready, Path A exists, marking rows are populated, and initially enabled transitions are highlighted.

User story: As a planner, I want to step one feasible transition so I can inspect how tokens move.
Expected behaviour: Clicking Step appends one breadcrumb, updates path metadata, and records the fired sequence in the audit receipt.
Testing notes: Verified by static interaction test with deterministic Math.random.

User story: As a planner, I want to reset the active path so I can restart a scenario cleanly.
Expected behaviour: Clicking Reset path clears the path back to M0, restores Ready status, and clears reachability output.

User story: As an analyst, I want S-invariants computed so I can inspect conserved resources or progress sums.
Expected behaviour: Clicking Show Conservation computes an invariant list, highlights the first invariant, and writes a summary result.

User story: As an analyst, I want to test whether a desired goal is reachable so I can validate the workflow model.
Expected behaviour: With goal {"complete":1}, Check Goal Reachability reports Reachable and shows a witness firing sequence.

User story: As an analyst, I want invalid goals rejected with helpful feedback so I can correct inputs quickly.
Expected behaviour: Unknown place ids or malformed JSON produce a Goal parse error status and explanatory output.

User story: As a planner, I want to click prior markings so I can compare earlier states without rebuilding the path.
Expected behaviour: Clicking a breadcrumb rewinds the active cursor and marks that breadcrumb active.

User story: As a planner, I want to fork feasible schedules so I can compare alternative firing sequences.
Expected behaviour: Clicking Branch Explorer prompts for an enabled transition, creates a new path tab, makes it active, and fires the chosen transition.
Testing notes: Verified by static interaction test with mocked prompt.

User story: As a planner, I want feedback when I click an unavailable transition so I understand why nothing fired.
Expected behaviour: Clicking a disabled transition sets Not enabled status without adding a breadcrumb.
